query: Consider the following context: The ability to endure extreme corrosion in challenging environments is reduced in stainless steel. This can be addressed by appropriate surface modification techniques to redefine the surface with the required properties. In that context, which method can be used for improved corrosion resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Applying a chromium-rich coating via physical vapor deposition (PVD) on stainless steel will improve its corrosion resistance in extreme environments.
generation.material_initial_state: Austenitic stainless steel (SS304) with a surface roughness of 0.1 μm, composed of 18% Cr, 8% Ni, and balance Fe, in the annealed condition
generation.intervention: Deposition of a 2 μm thick chromium-rich coating using PVD at 500°C
generation.conditions: Exposure to a 3.5% NaCl solution at 80°C for 100 hours, simulating a marine environment
generation.mechanism: The chromium-rich coating enhances the formation of a protective chromium oxide layer, which acts as a barrier to reduce the diffusion of corrosive species (such as Cl-) into the steel substrate, thereby decreasing the corrosion rate
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% reduction in corrosion rate compared to uncoated stainless steel, from 1.2 mm/year to 0.8 mm/year
generation.baseline: Uncoated SS304 exposed to the same conditions
generation.boundary: The coating thickness will be optimized within the 1-5 μm range to achieve the maximum corrosion resistance
generation.uncertainty: Variations in the composition of the stainless steel, the surface preparation before coating, and the specific conditions of the extreme environment may affect the outcome

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the corrosion rate of the coated stainless steel is not less than 0.5 mm/year lower than the uncoated sample after 100 hours of exposure, the hypothesis is falsified

system.state: prone to corrosion in extreme environments

frame.limitation: reduced ability to endure extreme corrosion
